extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, examiners, and legal practitioners advising on UK patent procedure under the Patents (Designs) Act (1883 era)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules under the Patents (Designs) Act for lodging and accepting specifications, opposition, sealing, provisional protection, patent dating and term, renewal payments, and amendment of specifications. Focuses on timelines, permitted grounds, procedures, and limits applicable to applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lodging complete specification within nine months
rubrics_metrics.description: If the complete specification be not lodged within nine months the application which includes the provisional specification will be deemed to be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment of a provisional specification does not make that specification public (Oxley v. Holden); a provisional specification only becomes public when accepted. Subject to sect. 7 sub-sects. (5) and (6), the same principle applies to provisional specifications abandoned under this Act. An application refused, abandoned, or void does not become public and therefore will not affect a subsequent application for a similar invention, except as provided in sect. 7 sub-sects. (5) and (6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of complete specification within twelve months
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a complete specification is accepted within twelve months from the date of application, then (save in the case of an appeal having been lodged against the refusal to accept) the application shall, at the expiration of those twelve months, become void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an appeal against refusal to accept is pending the law officer may direct when the patent shall be sealed. The requirement that a complete specification be lodged within nine months and accepted within twelve months implies timelines for appeals referenced in the section. Applications becoming void by non-acceptance are not made public (see related provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's comparison: prescribed form and substantial sameness
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller shall refer both provisional and complete specifications to an examiner to ascertain whether the complete specification has been prepared in the prescribed manner, and whether the invention particularly described in the complete specification is substantially the same as that described in the provisional specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner reports non-compliance the comptroller may refuse to accept the complete specification until amended to his satisfaction (subject to appeal to the law officer). Any substantial variation between the two specifications will invalidate the patent. A favourable examiner report is not conclusive; defendants may still allege material variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality: examiner reports and abandoned specs not published
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of examiners shall not in any case be published or be open to public inspection, and shall not be liable to production or inspection in any legal proceeding, other than an appeal to the law officer, except by court certificate authorising production for interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner reports may be used on appeal to the law officer. A court or officer having discovery power must certify desirability in the interests of justice before production is allowed. Abandoned specifications are not published and therefore generally do not bar subsequent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement and public inspection on acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: On the acceptance of the complete specification the comptroller shall advertise the acceptance; and the application and specification or specifications with the drawings (if any) shall be open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a complete specification is lodged in the first instance and accepted, it will be open to inspection as soon as it is advertised (Patents Rules, 26). Publication is typically in the Official Journal; inspection fees apply. The Patent Office opening hours and rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to grant — permitted grounds only
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may within two months from the date of the advertisement of the acceptance of a complete specification give notice of opposition to the grant of the patent on one of only these grounds: (1) the applicant obtained the invention from him (or his representative); (2) the invention has been patented in this country on an application of prior date; (3) an examiner has reported that the specification appears to comprise the same invention as that comprised in a specification bearing the same or similar title accompanying a previous application. No other ground of opposition is permitted before the comptroller under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section restricts opposition to these three grounds; objections such as want of utility or prior public user cannot be taken before the comptroller under this section (though Crown may refuse for other statutory reasons). Where both applications are made the same day, special rules and case law (In re Deering's Patent) apply. The prior-patent ground requires specification of title, number, and date of prior patent or it will not be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition practice and evidence timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: An opponent must give notice of opposition within two months of advertisement; within fourteen days after the expiration of those two months the opponent leaves affidavits in support and sends a list to the applicant; applicant leaves answering affidavits within fourteen days and furnishes a list; opponent may leave reply affidavits within seven days; no further evidence except by leave of the comptroller on consent or on special notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits taken abroad follow Patents Rules. The comptroller may enlarge time for lodging affidavits. The comptroller appoints the hearing (seven days' notice) and both parties pay hearing fees. Decisions are subject to appeal to the law officer; practice on appeals mirrors that under sect. 7. Forms, fees and detailed rules are in Patents Forms and Patents Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing of patent — automatic when no opposition or favourable decision, timing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no opposition, or if opposition is decided in favour of grant, the comptroller shall cause a patent to be sealed with the seal of the Patent Office. A patent shall be sealed as soon as may be, and not after the expiration of fifteen months from the date of application, except in specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions permitting later sealing: delays caused by appeals to the law officer (various appeals listed), opposition to grant (and appeals therefrom), and the death of the applicant (personal representative may obtain sealing within twelve months after death). Historically the law officer issued warrants for the great seal; sect. 12 substitutes the Patent Office seal and allows immediate sealing once objections disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of patent and limitations on proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be dated and sealed as of the date of application: provided that no proceedings shall be taken in respect of an infringement committed before the publication of the complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date of application is either day lodged personally or day of ordinary course of post (sect. 97). All applications made on same day for same invention are entitled to be sealed; prior case law allowed law officer to direct sealing as of any date between application and sealing, but current rule fixes date as application. Sealing of a patent on one application does not prevent sealing on a prior application for same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection between application/acceptance and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application for a patent has been accepted the invention may during the period between the date of the application and the date of sealing such patent be used and published without prejudice to the patent to be granted for the same; this protection is referred to as provisional protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional protection enables the applicant to use or publish the invention without causing loss of novelty for the subsequent patent. It does not give rights against the public — no action for infringement can be maintained for acts committed prior to the actual grant. Under sect. 18 and related provisions, once the patent is granted, actions for infringement may be maintained for acts committed after publication of the complete specification (see provisos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of acceptance (protection by complete specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the acceptance of a complete specification and until the date of sealing a patent in respect thereof, or the expiration of the time for sealing, the applicant shall have the like privileges and rights as if a patent for the invention had been sealed on the date of the acceptance: provided that an applicant shall not be entitled to institute any proceeding for infringement unless and until a patent for the invention has been granted to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives substantive provisional rights (subject to proviso that suit cannot be started until grant). Once a patent is granted, applicant can maintain action for acts of infringement previous to sealing provided they were committed after publication of the complete specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial extent and statutory term of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent when sealed shall have effect throughout the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man. The term limited in every patent for the duration thereof shall be fourteen years from its date (subject to renewal payments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent no longer applies to the Channel Islands. The patent ceases if the patentee fails to make prescribed payments within prescribed times (see renewals). Detailed fees and timing are in the schedules to the Act and Patents Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal/maintenance payments, notice, and enlargement of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee must pay prescribed renewal fees/take actions at prescribed times (various payment schedules and options described). Seven days at least before the expiration of any period the patentee must give notice to the comptroller in Form J transmitting the fee and certificate of payment. If the patentee fails to make a prescribed payment by accident, mistake, or inadvertence he may apply to the comptroller for enlargement of time; the comptroller may enlarge time on payment of prescribed enlargement fee (not exceeding ten pounds) and subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment options: lump sums (e.g., 50/. and 100/.) or yearly instalments with specified amounts for each instalment. Conditions on enlargement: (a) time not enlarged for more than three months; (b) fee to be paid; (c) where infringements occurred between expiry and enlargement, the Court may refuse to award damages in respect of such infringements. Application for extension in Form K must detail circumstances; comptroller may require substantiation (Patents Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of specification — process, advertisement, opposition, limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or patentee may from time to time by request in writing seek leave to amend his specification, including drawings, by way of disclaimer, correction, connection, or explanation, stating nature and reasons. The request and proposed amendment shall be advertised; any person may give notice of opposition within one month; the comptroller shall hear and decide subject to appeal to the law officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the law officer is required he shall hear the person making the request and any opposer and may determine whether and subject to what conditions the amendment shall be allowed. When no opposition is given the comptroller determines. If leave is refused the requester may appeal. No amendment shall be allowed that would make the specification claim an invention substantially larger than or substantially different from that claimed before amendment. Leave, when given, is conclusive except in case of fraud and the amendment is deemed to form part of the specification in all courts. Provisions do not apply while any action for infringement or legal proceeding relating to the patent is pending. Forms, fees and hearing procedures are set out in Patents Forms and Patents Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to oppose (who may oppose each ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different grounds of opposition have different practical availability: any person may take the second ground (invention patented in this country on prior application); any person may also take the third ground (examiner reported same invention) but practically this is restricted to the prior applicant because notice of such examiner's report is only given to applicants; the real or true inventor (or personal representative) may take the first ground (applicant obtained invention from him).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: disclosure to assistants or partners under obligation of secrecy is not a public disclosure; legal representatives have specific time-limits to apply under other provisions. The section narrows who can raise which objections before the comptroller; other remedies (e.g., actions) may remain available elsewhere.
